title: tighten-tenant-bootstrap-privileges-and-namespace-affinity-for-private-installer
author: Maya Thompson
commits: initial: add namespace-affinity annotation support to tenant-values and helm templates
tf: constrain rbac bootstrap module to cluster-scoped minimal roles + optional namespace whitelist
operator: gate bootstrap flow behind preflight validator and dry-run mode
tests: integration test for tenant isolation + idempotent re-bootstrap path
docs: onboarding guide updates and upgrade notes
description: Motivation: private deployments need stronger, automated guardrails during tenant bootstrap to avoid over-privileged cluster roles and accidental cross-tenant scheduling. This PR tightens the default bootstrap privileges, introduces a namespace-affinity mechanism so tenant workloads are pinned to a small set of namespaces, and wires a Helm + Terraform preflight + dry-run path into the installer. Summary of changes: 1) Helm: add tenant-level `namespaceAffinity` and `allowedNamespaces` fields to charts/private values with validation schema and a templated RoleBinding patch that restricts tenant service account bindings to allowed namespaces; 2) Terraform: update rbac-bootstrap module to create minimal clusterrole templates and an opt-in `clusterWide` flag, move broad ClusterRoleBinding creation into a conditional, and expose a migration helper to convert existing bindings; 3) Bootstrap operator: add a preflight validator that runs a dry-run RBAC plan using the new Terraform helper, validates namespace affinity constraints, and fails fast with actionable errors; 4) Tests/docs: add integration tests for idempotent re-bootstrap, tenant isolation tests that simulate namespace drift, and update onboarding docs with upgrade/migration steps. Rollout and upgrade strategy: default behavior is backwards-compatible — existing installs continue to use the previous bootstrap path unless the operator is configured with `enforceNamespaceAffinity=true` or the Terraform module `migrate_bindings=true` is enabled. The PR includes a migration helper and a documented, manual migration path for clusters with existing tenants. For safety this change includes a non-blocking preflight stage in CI and a gated operator flag for enforcement. Checklist: ensure terraform state snapshots, run the migration-helper in dry-run against staging, run integration suite (included), update customer-facing upgrade notes. Why unique: this combines helm-level scheduling guardrails with terraform-level RBAC hardening and ties them to an operator preflight so the change can be rolled out gradually without accidental privilege escalation.
review_comments: Arjun: Can we add a telemetry event when preflight fails so SRE can surface tenant misconfigurations?
Maya: Added `preflight.failures.count` metric and documented it in metrics.yml in a follow-up commit.
Lena: The migration helper needs to be idempotent; what happens if it runs twice?
Maya: Migration helper now records a migration-timestamp annotation and is guarded with optimistic locking; updated tests to cover double-run.
Hugo: Please ensure the default `allowedNamespaces` list is empty (deny-by-default), otherwise this could open namespaces inadvertently.
Maya: Default changed to empty; installer will create namespaces when `createNamespaces=true` is set in tenant-values. CI smoke verifies default deny behavior.
Arjun: CI flaked once on k8s v1.26 RBAC canonicalization; I re-ran the job and it passed — consider a follow-up to canonicalize API group ordering.
Lena: Approving now; leaving a note that on-prem SRE should schedule a dry-run migration before upgrade.
release_notes: Hardened tenant bootstrap for private installs: added namespace-affinity and allowedNamespaces controls to Helm chart; tightened Terraform rbac-bootstrap to produce minimal default privileges and an opt-in migration path; added operator preflight validator and dry-run support; updated onboarding docs and integration tests. Upgrade notes: run migration-helper in staging and enable enforcement behind the operator flag; default behavior is opt-in.
